Theorem 1.Theorem:
If $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}, b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ are real or complex numbers, and

$$
S_{i}=a_{1}+a_{2}+\ldots+a_{i}, i=1,2, \ldots, n
$$

then

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} S_{i}\left(b_{i}-b_{i+1}\right)+S_{n} b_{n}
$$

Theorem 2.Theorem:
If $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ are nonnegative real numbers, then

$$
\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} \geq\left(a_{1} a_{2} \ldots a_{n}\right)^{\frac{1}{n}}
$$

with equality if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\ldots=a_{n}$. This inequality is a special case of the Power Mean Inequality.

Theorem 3.Theorem:
If $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ are positive real numbers, then

$$
\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} \geq \frac{1}{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_{i}}}
$$

with equality if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\ldots=a_{n}$. This inequality is a special case of the Power Mean Inequality.

Theorem 4.Theorem: For any real numbers $x>-1$ and $a>1$ we have $(1+x)^{a} \geq 1+a x$.

Theorem 6.Theorem:
If $a, b$ are real numbers, $a<b$, and $f, g:[a, b] \rightarrow R$ are integrable functions, then

$$
\left(\int_{a}^{b} f(x) g(x) d x\right)^{2} \leq\left(\int_{a}^{b} f^{2}(x) d x\right) \cdot\left(\int_{a}^{b} g^{2}(x) d x\right)
$$

Theorem 8.Theorem:
If $a, b$ are real numbers, $a<b$, and $f, g:[a, b] \rightarrow R$ are integrable functions and having the same monotonicity, then

$$
(b-a) \int_{a}^{b} f(x) g(x) d x \geq \int_{a}^{b} f(x) d x \cdot \int_{a}^{b} g(x) d x
$$

and if one is increasing, while the other is decreasing the reversed inequality is true.

Theorem 9.Theorem:
A real-valued function $f$ defined on an interval $I$ of real numbers is convex if, for any $x, y$ in $I$ and any nonnegative numbers $\alpha, \beta$ with sum 1 ,

$$
f(\alpha x+\beta y) \leq \alpha f(x)+\beta f(y)
$$

Theorem 10.Theorem:
A function $f(x)$ is concave up (down) on $[a, b] \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ if $f(x)$ lies under (over) the line connecting $\left(a_{1}, f\left(a_{1}\right)\right)$ and $\left(b_{1}, f\left(b_{1}\right)\right)$ for all

$$
a \leq a_{1}<x<b_{1} \leq b
$$

A function $g(x)$ is concave up (down) on the Euclidean plane if it is concave up (down) on each line in the plane, where we identify the line naturally
with $\mathbb{R}$.
Concave up and down functions are also called convex and concave, respectively.
If $f$ is concave up on an interval $[a, b]$ and $\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2}, \ldots, \lambda_{n}$ are nonnegative numbers wit sum equal to 1 , then
$\lambda_{1} f\left(x_{1}\right)+\lambda_{2} f\left(x_{2}\right)+\ldots+\lambda_{n} f\left(x_{n}\right) \geq f\left(\lambda_{1} x_{1}+\lambda_{2} x_{2}+\ldots+\lambda_{n} x_{n}\right)$
for any $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}$ in the interval $[a, b]$. If the function is concave down, the inequality is reversed. This is Jensen's Inequality.

Theorem 11.Theorem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Given a function $f$ of $n$ variables, define the cyclic sum of variables $\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}\right)$ as

$$
\begin{gathered}
\sum_{c y c} f\left(x_{1}, x_{3}, \ldots, x_{n}\right)=f\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}\right)+f\left(x_{2}, x_{3}, \ldots, x_{n}, x_{1}\right) \\
+\ldots+f\left(a_{n}, a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n-1}\right)
\end{gathered}
$$

Theorem 12.Theorem:
If $r, s$ are positive real numbers such that $\frac{1}{r}+\frac{1}{s}=1$, then for any positive real numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$,
$b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$

$$
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i}}{n} \leq\left(\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{r}}{n}\right)^{\frac{1}{r}} \cdot\left(\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{s}}{n}\right)^{\frac{1}{s}}
$$

Theorem 13.Theorem:
If $p_{1}, p_{2}, \ldots, p_{n}, a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}, b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ are positive real numbers with $p_{1}+p_{2}+\ldots+p_{n}=1$, then

$$
\prod_{i=1}^{n}\left(a_{i}+b_{i}\right)^{p_{i}} \geq \prod_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{p_{i}}+\prod_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{p_{i}}
$$

Theorem 14.Theorem:
For any positive real numbers $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}$

$$
S_{1} \geq S_{2} \geq \ldots \geq S_{n}
$$

where

$$
S_{k}=\sqrt[k]{\frac{\sum_{1 \leq i_{1}<i_{2}<\ldots<i_{k} \leq n} x_{i_{1}} \cdot x_{i_{2}} \cdot \ldots \cdot x_{i_{k}}}{\binom{n}{k}}}
$$

Theorem 15.Theorem:
For any real number $r \geq 1$ and any positive real numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}, b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$

$$
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(a_{i}+b_{i}\right)^{r}\right)^{\frac{1}{r}} \leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{r}\right)^{\frac{1}{r}}+\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{r}\right)^{\frac{1}{r}}
$$

Theorem 16.Theorem: For any positive real numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ with sum equal to 1 , and any positive real numbers $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}$, we define $M_{r}=\left(a_{1} x_{1}^{r}+a_{2} x_{2}^{r}+\right.$ $\left.\ldots+a_{n} x_{n}^{r}\right)^{\frac{1}{r}}$ if $r$ is a non-zero real and $M_{0}=x_{1}^{a_{1}} x_{2}^{a_{2}} \ldots x_{n}^{a_{n}}, M_{\infty}=$ $\max \left\{x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}\right\}, M_{-\infty}=\min \left\{x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}\right\}$. Then for any reals $s \leq t$ we have $M_{-\infty} \leq M_{s} \leq M_{t} \leq M_{\infty}$.

Theorem 17.Theorem:
If $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ are nonnegative real numbers, then

$$
\sqrt{\frac{a_{1}^{2}+a_{2}^{2}+\ldots+a_{n}^{2}}{n}} \geq \frac{a_{1}+a_{2}+\ldots+a_{n}}{n}
$$

with equality if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\ldots=a_{n}$.

Theorem 19.Theorem:
For any nonnegative real numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$

$$
(n-1) \sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{k}^{n}+n \prod_{k=1}^{n} a_{k} \geq\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{k}\right) \cdot\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{k}^{n-1}\right)
$$

Theorem 21.Theorem:
For any nonnegative real numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$, if $w_{1}, w_{2}, \ldots, w_{n}$ are nonnegative real numbers (weights) with sum 1 , then

$$
w_{1} a_{1}+w_{2} a_{2}+\ldots+w_{n} a_{n} \geq a_{1}^{w_{1}} a_{2}^{w_{2}} \ldots a_{n}^{w_{n}}
$$

with equality if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\ldots=a_{n}$.

Theorem 23.Theorem:
Let $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}^{+}$, and let us denote
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q M & =\sqrt{\frac{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}{3}}, \quad A M=\frac{a+b+c}{3}, \quad G M=\sqrt[3]{a b c} \text { and } \\
H M & =\frac{3}{\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Then
$$
Q M \geq A M \geq G M \geq H M
$$

Equalities occur if and only if $a=b=c$.

Theorem 26.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ and $b_{1}, b_{2}$, $\ldots, b_{n}$ be real numbers. Then we have
$$
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{2}\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{2}\right) \geq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i}\right)^{2}
$$
i.e.
$$
\left(a_{1}^{2}+a_{2}^{2}+\cdots+a_{n}^{2}\right)\left(b_{1}^{2}+b_{2}^{2}+\cdots+b_{n}^{2}\right) \geq\left(a_{1} b_{1}+a_{2} b_{2}+\cdots+a_{n} b_{n}\right)^{2}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if the sequences $\left(a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}\right)$ and $\left(b_{1}, b_{2}\right.$, $\ldots, b_{n}$ ) are proportional, i.e. $\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}$.

Theorem 27.Theorem:
Let $a, b, x, y$ be real numbers and $x, y>0$. Then we have
$$
\text { (1) } \frac{a^{2}}{x}+\frac{b^{2}}{y} \geq \frac{(a+b)^{2}}{x+y}, \quad \text { (2) } \frac{a^{2}}{x}+\frac{b^{2}}{y}+\frac{c^{2}}{z} \geq \frac{(a+b+c)^{2}}{x+y+z} \text {. }
$$

Theorem 28.Theorem:
Let $a_{1} \leq a_{2} \leq \cdots \leq a_{n}$ and $b_{1} \leq b_{2} \leq$ $\cdots \leq b_{n}$ be real numbers. Then we have
$$
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}\right) \leq n \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i}
$$
i.e.
$$
\left(a_{1}+a_{2}+\cdots+a_{n}\right)\left(b_{1}+b_{2}+\cdots+b_{n}\right) \leq n\left(a_{1} b_{1}+a_{2} b_{2}+\cdots+a_{n} b_{n}\right)
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\cdots=a_{n}$ or $b_{1}=b_{2}=\cdots=b_{n}$.

Theorem 29.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n} ; b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ be real numbers such that $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}>0$. Then
$$
\frac{a_{1}^{2}}{b_{1}}+\frac{a_{2}^{2}}{b_{2}}+\cdots+\frac{a_{n}^{2}}{b_{n}} \geq \frac{\left(a_{1}+a_{2}+\cdots+a_{n}\right)^{2}}{b_{1}+b_{2}+\cdots+b_{n}}
$$
with equality if and only if $\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}$.

Theorem 30.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ be non-negative real numbers, and let $n$ be a positive integer. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
& (n-1)\left(a_{1}^{n}+a_{2}^{n}+\cdots+a_{n}^{n}\right)+n a_{1} a_{2} \cdots a_{n} \\
& \quad \geq\left(a_{1}+a_{2}+\cdots+a_{n}\right)\left(a_{1}^{n-1}+a_{2}^{n-1}+\cdots+a_{n}^{n-1}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Theorem 32.Theorem:
Let $a, b, c$ and $x, y, z$ be positive real numbers. Then
$$
\frac{x}{y+z}(b+c)+\frac{y}{z+x}(c+a)+\frac{z}{x+y}(a+b) \geq \sqrt{3(a b+b c+c a)}
$$

Theorem 35.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ be positive real numbers. The numbers
$$
\begin{aligned}
& Q M=\sqrt{\frac{a_{1}^{2}+a_{2}^{2}+\cdots+a_{n}^{2}}{n}}, \quad A M=\frac{a_{1}+a_{2}+\cdots+a_{n}}{n} \\
& G M=\sqrt[n]{a_{1} a_{2} \cdots a_{n}} \quad \text { and } \quad H M=\frac{n}{\frac{1}{a_{1}}+\frac{1}{a_{2}}+\cdots+\frac{1}{a_{n}}}
\end{aligned}
$$
are called the quadratic, arithmetic, geometric and harmonic mean for the numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$, respectively, and we have
$$
Q M \geq A M \geq G M \geq H M
$$

Equalities occur if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\cdots=a_{n}$.

Theorem 37.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ be real numbers and let $\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}\right)$ be a permutation of $\left(a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}\right)$. Then
$$
a_{1}^{2}+a_{2}^{2}+\cdots+a_{n}^{2} \geq a_{1} x_{1}+a_{2} x_{2}+\cdots+a_{n} x_{n}
$$

Theorem 38.Theorem: Let $f:(a, b) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ and for any $x \in(a, b)$ suppose there exists a second derivative $f^{\prime \prime}(x)$. The function $f(x)$ is convex on $(a, b)$ if and only if for each $x \in(a, b)$ we have $f^{\prime \prime}(x) \geq 0$. If $f^{\prime \prime}(x)>0$ for each $x \in(a, b)$, then $f$ is strictly convex on $(a, b)$.

Theorem 39.Theorem: Let $f_{1}, f_{2}, \ldots, f_{n}$ be convex functions on $(a, b)$. Then the function $c_{1} f_{1}+c_{2} f_{2}+\cdots+c_{n} f_{n}$ is also convex on $(a, b)$, for any $c_{1}, c_{2}, \ldots, c_{n} \in$ $(0, \infty)$

Theorem 41.Theorem:
Let $f:[a, b] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a convex function on the interval $[a, b]$. Then for any $x, y, z \in[a, b]$ we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
& f\left(\frac{x+y+z}{3}\right)+\frac{f(x)+f(y)+f(z)}{3} \\
& \quad \geq \frac{2}{3}\left(f\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)+f\left(\frac{y+z}{2}\right)+f\left(\frac{z+x}{2}\right)\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Theorem 42.Theorem:
Let $f:[a, b] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be $a$ convex function on the interval $[a, b]$ and $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n} \in[a, b]$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
& f\left(a_{1}\right)+f\left(a_{2}\right)+\cdots+f\left(a_{n}\right)+n(n-2) f(a) \\
& \quad \geq(n-1)\left(f\left(b_{1}\right)+f\left(b_{2}\right)+\cdots+f\left(b_{n}\right)\right)
\end{aligned}
$$
where $a=\frac{a_{1}+a_{2}+\cdots+a_{n}}{n}$, and $b_{i}=\frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{i \neq j} a_{j}$ for all $i$.

Theorem 44.Theorem:
Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in(0, \pi)$. Then $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are the angles of a triangle if and only if
$$
\tan \frac{\alpha}{2} \tan \frac{\beta}{2}+\tan \frac{\beta}{2} \tan \frac{\gamma}{2}+\tan \frac{\alpha}{2} \tan \frac{\gamma}{2}=1
$$

Theorem 45.Theorem:
Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in(0, \pi)$. Then $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are the angles of a triangle if and only if
$$
\sin ^{2} \frac{\alpha}{2}+\sin ^{2} \frac{\beta}{2}+\sin ^{2} \frac{\gamma}{2}+2 \sin \frac{\alpha}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\beta}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\gamma}{2}=1
$$

Theorem 46.Theorem: Let $a, b>0$ and $p, q>1$ be real numbers such that $1 / p+1 / q=1$. Then $a b \leq \frac{a^{p}}{p}+\frac{b^{q}}{q}$. Equality occurs if and only if $a^{p}=b^{q}$.

Theorem 48.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n} ; b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ be positive real numbers and $p, q>1$ be such that $1 / p+1 / q=1$.
Then
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i} \leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{q}\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $\frac{a_{1}^{p}}{b_{1}^{q}}=\frac{a_{2}^{p}}{b_{2}^{q}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}^{p}}{b_{n}^{q}}$.

Theorem 49.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n} ; b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots$, $b_{n} ; m_{1}, m_{2}, \ldots, m_{n}$ be three sequences of positive real numbers and $p, q>1$ be such that $1 / p+1 / q=1$.
Then
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i} m_{i} \leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{p} m_{i}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{q} m_{i}\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}
$$

Equality occurs iff $\frac{a_{1}^{p}}{b_{1}^{q}}=\frac{a_{2}^{p}}{b_{2}^{q}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}^{p}}{b_{n}^{q}}$.

Theorem 50.Theorem:
Let $a_{i j}, i=1,2, \ldots, m ; j=$ $1,2, \ldots, n$, be positive real numbers, and $\alpha_{1}, \alpha_{2}, \ldots, \alpha_{n}$ be positive real numbers such that $\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}+\cdots+\alpha_{n}=1$.
Then
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\prod_{j=1}^{m} a_{i j}^{\alpha_{j}}\right) \leq \prod_{j=1}^{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m} a_{i j}\right)^{\alpha_{j}}
$$

Theorem 51.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n} ; b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ be positive real numbers and $p>1$. Then
$$
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(a_{i}+b_{i}\right)^{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}+\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}$.

Theorem 52.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n} ; b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ be positive real numbers and $p>1$. Then
$$
\left(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}\right)^{p}+\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}\right)^{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \leq \sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(a_{i}^{p}+b_{i}^{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}$.

Theorem 53.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ and $b_{1}, b_{2}$, $\ldots, b_{n}$ be positive real numbers. Then
$$
\sqrt[n]{a_{1} a_{2} \cdots a_{n}}+\sqrt[n]{b_{1} b_{2} \cdots b_{n}} \leq \sqrt[n]{\left(a_{1}+b_{1}\right)\left(a_{2}+b_{2}\right) \cdots\left(a_{n}+b_{n}\right)}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}$.

Theorem 54.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n} ; b_{1}, b_{2}$, $\ldots, b_{n} ; m_{1}, m_{2}, \ldots, m_{n}$ be three sequences of positive real numbers and let $p>1$. Then
$$
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(a_{i}+b_{i}\right)^{p} m_{i}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{p} m_{i}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}+\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{p} m_{i}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}$.

Theorem 55.Theorem:
Let $a_{i}, b_{i} \in \mathbb{R}, i=$ $1,2, \ldots, n$, be real numbers and let $m_{i} \in \mathbb{R}^{+}, i=1,2, \ldots, n$. Then we have the inequality
$$
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i} m_{i}\right)^{2} \leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i}^{2} m_{i}\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i}^{2} m_{i}\right)
$$

Equality occurs iff $\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}=\frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}=\cdots=\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}$.

Theorem 57.Theorem:
Let $a_{1} \leq a_{2} \leq \cdots \leq a_{n}$; $b_{1} \leq b_{2} \leq \cdots \leq b_{n}$ be real numbers and let $m_{1}, m_{2}, \ldots, m_{n}$ be non-negative real numbers such that $m_{1}+m_{2}+\cdots+m_{n}=1$.
Then
$$
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} m_{i}\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_{i} m_{i}\right) \leq \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{i} b_{i} m_{i}
$$

Equality occurs iff $a_{1}=a_{2}=\cdots=a_{n}$ or $b_{1}=b_{2}=\cdots=b_{n}$.

Theorem 58.Theorem: Let $a=\left(a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}\right)$ be a sequence of positive real numbers and $r \neq 0$ be real number. Then $M_{r}(a) \leq$ $M_{s}(a)$, for any real numbers $r \leq s$.

Theorem 59.Theorem:
Let $a=\left(a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}\right)$ be a sequence of positive real numbers, and let $m=\left(m_{1}, m_{2}, \ldots, m_{n}\right)$ also be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $m_{1}+m_{2}+\cdots+m_{n}=1$.
Then for each $r \leq s$ we have
$$
M_{r}^{m}(a) \leq M_{s}^{m}(a)
$$
i.e.
$$
\left(m_{1} a_{1}^{r}+m_{2} a_{2}^{r}+\cdots+m_{n} a_{n}^{r}\right)^{\frac{1}{r}} \leq\left(m_{1} a_{1}^{s}+m_{2} a_{2}^{s}+\cdots+m_{n} a_{n}^{s}\right)^{\frac{1}{s}}
$$

Theorem 60.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}>0$ be arbitrary real numbers. Then for each $k=1,2, \ldots, n-1$, we have
$$
p_{k-1} p_{k+1} \leq p_{k}^{2}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\cdots=a_{n}$.

Theorem 61.Theorem:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}>0$. Then
$$
p_{1} \geq p_{2}^{\frac{1}{2}} \geq \cdots \geq p_{k}^{\frac{1}{k}} \geq \cdots \geq p_{n}^{\frac{1}{n}}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $a_{1}=a_{2}=\cdots=a_{n}$.

Theorem 62.Theorem:
Let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\beta>0$. Then we have
$$
T[\alpha+2 \beta, 0,0]+T[\alpha, \beta, \beta] \geq 2 T[\alpha+\beta, \beta, 0]
$$

Theorem 63.Theorem:
Let $x, y, z$ and $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers such that $a \geq$ $b \geq c$ or $a \leq b \leq c$. Then we have
$$
a(x-y)(x-z)+b(y-x)(y-z)+c(z-x)(z-y) \geq 0
$$

Theorem 64.Theorem:
Let $x, y, z \geq 0$ be real numbers and let $t \in \mathbb{R}$. Then we have
$$
x^{t}(x-y)(x-z)+y^{t}(y-x)(y-z)+z^{t}(z-x)(z-y) \geq 0
$$
with equality if and only if $x=y=z$ or $x=y, z=0$ (up to permutation).

Theorem 65.Theorem: Let $x, y, z>0$. Then $3 x y z+x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{3} \geq 2\left((x y)^{3 / 2}+\right.$ $\left.(y z)^{3 / 2}+(z x)^{3 / 2}\right)$

Theorem 66.Theorem:
Let $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}$ be a sequence of non-negative real numbers and let $\left(\alpha_{i}\right)$ and $\left(\beta_{i}\right)$ be sequences of positive real numbers such that $\left(\beta_{i}\right) \prec\left(\alpha_{i}\right)$. Then
$$
T\left[\beta_{i}\right] \leq T\left[\alpha_{i}\right]
$$

Equality occurs iff $\left(\alpha_{i}\right)=\left(\beta_{i}\right)$ or $x_{1}=x_{2}=\cdots=x_{n}$.

Theorem 67.Theorem:
Let $k \in(0,3]$. Then for any $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}^{+}$we have
$$
(3-k)+k(a b c)^{2 / k}+a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2} \geq 2(a b+b c+c a)
$$

Theorem 68.Theorem:
Let $f: I \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a convex function on the interval $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and let $\left(a_{i}\right)_{i=1}^{n},\left(b_{i}\right)_{i=1}^{n}$, where $a_{i}, b_{i} \in I, i=$ $1,2, \ldots, n$, are two sequences, such that $\left(a_{i}\right) \succ\left(b_{i}\right)$. Then
$$
f\left(a_{1}\right)+f\left(a_{2}\right)+\cdots+f\left(a_{n}\right) \geq f\left(b_{1}\right)+f\left(b_{2}\right)+\cdots+f\left(b_{n}\right)
$$

Theorem 69.Theorem:
Let $f:(a, b) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function on $(a, b)$.
If, for all $x \in(a, b), f^{\prime}(x) \geq 0$, then $f$ is a monotone increasing function on the interval $(a, b)$.

If, for all $x \in(a, b)$, we have $f^{\prime}(x) \leq 0$, then $f$ is a monotone decreasing function on the interval $(a, b)$.
If we have strict inequalities then $f$ is a strictly increasing, respectively, strictly decreasing function on $(a, b)$.

Theorem 71.Theorem:
Let $x, y, z \geq 0$ and $p=x+y+z, q=x y+y z+z x, r=x y z$. Then we have:
$$
N_{1}: p^{3}-4 p q+9 r \geq 0, \quad N_{2}: p^{4}-5 p^{2} q+4 q^{2}+6 p r \geq 0
$$

Theorem 72.Theorem:
Let $x, y, z \geq 0$, and $p=x+y+z, q=x y+y z+z x, r=x y z$.
Then we have the following inequalities:
$$
\begin{array}{ll}
N_{3}: p q-9 r \geq 0, & N_{9}: p^{4}+3 q^{2} \geq 4 p^{2} q \\
N_{4}: p^{2} \geq 3 q, & N_{10}: 2 p^{3}+9 r^{2} \geq 7 p q r \\
N_{5}: p^{3} \geq 27 r, & N_{11}: p^{2} q+3 p r \geq 4 q^{2} \\
N_{6}: q^{3} \geq 27 r^{2}, & N_{12}: q^{3}+9 r^{2} \geq 4 p q r \\
N_{7}: q^{2} \geq 3 p r, & N_{13}: p q^{2} \geq 2 p^{2} r+3 q r \\
N_{8}: 2 p^{3}+9 r \geq 7 p q, &
\end{array}
$$

Theorem 73.Theorem:
Let $a, b, c$ be real numbers such that $a+b+c=1$ and let
$$
a b+b c+c a=\frac{1-q^{2}}{3} \quad(q \geq 0)
$$

Then we have the following inequalities
$$
\frac{(1+q)^{2}(1-2 q)}{27} \leq a b c \leq \frac{(1-q)^{2}(1+2 q)}{27}
$$

Theorem 74.Theorem:
Let $a, b, c$ be real numbers such that $a+b+$ $c=p$.
Let $a b+b c+c a=\frac{p^{2}-q^{2}}{3},(q \geq 0)$ and $a b c=r$.
Then
$$
\frac{(p+q)^{2}(p-2 q)}{27} \leq r \leq \frac{(p-q)^{2}(p+2 q)}{27}
$$

Equality occurs if and only if $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=0$.

Theorem 75.Theorem: If the function $f(a b c, a b+b c+c a, a+b+c)$ is monotonic then $f$ achieves it's maximum and minimum values on $\mathbb{R}$ when $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=0$, and on $\mathbb{R}^{+}$when $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=0$ or $a b c=0$.

Theorem 76.Theorem: If the function $f(a b c, a b+b c+c a, a+b+c)$ is a convex function then it achieves it's maximum and minimum values on $\mathbb{R}$ when $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=0$, and on $\mathbb{R}^{+}$when $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=0$ or $a b c=0$.

Theorem 77.Theorem: If the function $f(a b c, a b+b c+c a, a+b+c)$ is a concave function then it achieves it's maximum and minimum values on $\mathbb{R}$ when $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=0$, and on $\mathbb{R}^{+}$when $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=0$ or $a b c=0$.

Theorem 78.Theorem:
Consider the expression $S=S_{a}(b-c)^{2}+$ $S_{b}(a-c)^{2}+S_{c}(a-b)^{2}$, where $S_{a}, S_{b}, S_{c}$ are functions of $a, b, c$.
$1^{\circ}$ If $S_{a}, S_{b}, S_{c} \geq 0$ then $S \geq 0$.
$2^{\circ}$ If $a \geq b \geq c$ or $a \leq b \leq c$ and $S_{b}, S_{b}+S_{a}, S_{b}+S_{c} \geq 0$ then $S \geq 0$.
$3^{\circ}$ If $a \geq b \geq c$ or $a \leq b \leq c$ and $S_{a}, S_{c}, S_{a}+2 S_{b}, S_{c}+2 S_{b} \geq 0$ then $S \geq 0$.
$4^{\circ}$ If $a \geq b \geq c$ and $S_{b}, S_{c}, a^{2} S_{b}+b^{2} S_{a} \geq 0$ then $S \geq 0$.
$5^{\circ}$ If $S_{a}+S_{b} \geq 0$ or $S_{b}+S_{c} \geq 0$ or $S_{c}+S_{a} \geq 0\left(S_{a}+S_{b}+S_{c} \geq 0\right)$ and $S_{a} S_{b}+S_{b} S_{c}+S_{c} S_{a} \geq 0$ then $S \geq 0$.

Theorem 79.Theorem:
Let $F: I \subset \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a symmetric, continuous, function satisfying $F\left(a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}\right) \geq F\left(b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}\right)$, where the sequence $\left(b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}\right)$ is a sequence obtained from the sequence $\left(a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}\right)$ by some predefined transformation ( $a \Delta$-transformation).
Then we have $F\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}\right) \geq F(x, x, \ldots, x)$, with $x=\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}+\cdots+x_{n}}{n}$.

Theorem 80.Theorem: Let $f\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{m}\right)$ be a continuous and differentiable function on $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{m}$, and let $g_{i}\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{m}\right)$ $=0, i=1,2, \ldots, k$, where $(k<m)$ are the conditions that must be satisfied. Then the maximum or minimum values of $f$ with the conditions $g_{i}\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots\right.$, $\left.x_{m}\right)=0, i=1,2, \ldots, k$, occur at the bounds of the interval $I$ or occur at the points at which the partial derivatives (according to the variables $\left.x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{m}\right)$ of the function $L=f-\sum_{i=1}^{k} \lambda_{i} g_{i}$, are all zero.

Theorem 81.Theorem: Let $a, b, c$ be the sides of a triangle. Then the area of the triangle is given by $A=\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$, where $s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}$ is the semiperimeter of the triangle.

Theorem 82.Theorem: If a triangle in the plane has side lengths $a, b$ and $c$ and area $T$, then $$a^2+b^2+c^2 \geq (a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2 + 4\sqrt{3}T$$.

Theorem 83.Theorem: Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers. Then $$\frac{a}{b+c}+\frac{b}{c+a}+\frac{c}{a+b}\geq\frac{3}{2}$$.
